title: Notion says a vendor kept chat text it had promised not to keep
friendlyTitle: Notion says a vendor kept chat text from some workspaces
summary: Notion says Fireworks AI notified it of a security incident affecting fewer than 1 percent of workspaces. The exposed text is Notion AI chat input and output that Notion had sent to Fireworks for the Insights feature. On 3 November, Notion says it disconnected Fireworks, deleted the data held there, stopped sending traffic, and halted training runs. Insights is off while Notion investigates. Meeting-note audio was not affected unless someone pasted it into a chat.
friendlySummary: Notion says Fireworks AI told it about a security incident. Fewer than 1 percent of workspaces were affected. The exposed text is what people typed into Notion AI, and what the model wrote back, for a feature called Insights. On 3 November, Notion says it cut Fireworks off, deleted the data held there, and stopped training runs. Meeting audio was not taken unless someone pasted it into a chat.
whyItMatters: If neither you nor a workspace owner has heard from Notion, the company says it has not identified your workspace as affected. The investigation is still open. Affected owners can review the text on a desktop browser under the question-mark menu, then Security incident review. If anyone pasted a password or an API key into Notion AI, rotate it. Notion says a zero-retention promise did not cover Insights, because Notion itself stored those chats to run the feature, and the vendor retained data anyway.
friendlyWhyItMatters: If Notion has not emailed you or your workspace owner, it says your workspace was not identified as affected. The check is not finished. Affected owners can review the text on a computer, not in the phone app, under the question-mark menu. If anyone pasted a password or a key into Notion AI, change it. A promise not to keep data did not cover this feature, because Notion stored the chats to run it.
